title: Perf run 20261019-1841
heading: No speed win this run: the partial-frame code from the last run now has tests that fail when it breaks
meta:
This general run kept 18 commits of tests, fixes and docs, and no speed change. They are on branch improve/20261019-1841, from base 30c9407, with origin/main (ff08b93) merged in before the final checks.

Most of the run went to the code the last run added, which redraws only the changed part of a frame while the camera rests. Its unit tests now fail on 16 one-line breaks that the base's tests let through, and its e2e test now bounds how much of the canvas each frame redraws. Three small fixes ship with it: a failed search now logs its stack on every browser, game addresses tell search engines not to index them, and the hidden-object list now lives with the rest of the partial-frame state.In the final A/B of the branch against main as merged, no primary row was called better or worse (×0.995 over 16 rows).

needs.intro: Nothing here blocks the merge. All three items are information the skill asks for.

items.title: Information: the 1.2× target is not met
items.body: No change this run aimed at a primary row. The orchestrator put the last run's new partial-frame code and its tests first, and the one speed idea tried (skipping the damage walk on frames drawn whole, ledger 1841:PS1) changed no row: 0 of 3 primary rows called, and the rows it aimed at leaned slower. The next speed leads (DR12, CC2, FM1, QK1, KP1, DR2) are still at the top of the ledger for the next speed run.

items.title: The long view
items.body: Not re-measured this run. Run 20261018-1719 measured its head 2.41 times as fast as the first recorded run's base over 13 rows (ab-20261018-1719-vs-first-run.md).

changed.intro: Each change is its own commit. Every check below was shown to fail on broken code: node bench/loop/tools/mutate.mjs bench/loop/tools/breaks-20261019-1841.json applies each of 16 one-line breaks alone and runs its tests; on the branch all 16 fail, and with --at 30c9407 12 pass the base's tests and 4 are in code that is new on the branch.

items.title: The partial-frame tests fail on broken code (6a4e713, 68dd4d3, 487b1a2, 887dee3, 67bcbab)
items.body: damage.test.ts now fails when the frame signature leaves out the draw order, a vector's z or a colour; when two screen rects are united with the wrong height; when rects are kept after a frame drawn whole; when a sprite's reach ignores its centre; and when lines are not walked. It also pins the kinds of object three.js draws, read from the installed WebGLRenderer.js. backdropCache.test.tsx now tests a frame drawn in part for the first time: the scissor in CSS pixels at pixel ratios 1, 1.5 and 2.625, culling, and hidden objects shown again, by the copy and, should the copy not be drawn, at the next frame's start. framePacer.test.tsx fails if the pacer leaves the scissor on.

items.title: The e2e test bounds how much each partial frame redraws (ddd2eb6)
items.body: e2e/damage.spec.ts now records the share of the canvas each of the board's own frames redraws. It expects more than 20 frames, more than 3 in 4 drawn in part, and a median share under 0.25. Locally the median read 0.04 on desktop and 0.06 on a phone, 0.21 at most. With every partial frame's scissor set to the whole canvas, both tests fail.

items.title: The hidden-object list moved onto the partial-frame state (54e6bd1, DR11)
items.body: Objects hidden for a frame drawn in part are now shown again by the backdrop copy as three.js draws it, so the frame pacer no longer needs to know about them and framePacer.tsx no longer imports from the scene. Production lines +13 −13. A render by anything other than the pacer can no longer leave the tower hidden. The test's "nothing left hidden after a frame" fails on the base's code. e2e/damage.spec.ts (pixel for pixel against whole frames, desktop and phone) passes.

items.title: A failed search logs where it failed, on every browser (534e140, 1597cdd, WS1)
items.body: The search's worker now sends the error's stack with its message, so the page's log says where the search failed. Outside Chrome, a stack holds only the frames, so the reply puts the message first there. worker.test.ts fails on the base's reply and on a stack-only reply. The worker now counts toward the computer player's 90% coverage gate.

items.title: Game addresses are kept out of search results (65aa639, d0faaf7, XR1)
items.body: A game's address is the only key to its seats. public/_headers now sends X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow on /game/*. Production served no such header (checked with curl -I). preview.config.test.ts reads the file as Cloudflare Pages does and fails on the base. ARCHITECTURE.md names the rule.

items.title: Screen-reader rules now run as checks (e9a6a86, b360245, bb30cc8, E11)
items.body: CLAUDE.md says the move box is the first Tab stop and the announcer and hidden move list are never display: none. playMove.spec.ts now presses Tab once (it allowed five) and checks that the announcer, the move list's nav and the list itself are rendered. A button put before the move box fails it, and so does hiding any of the three in index.css.

items.title: The computer's bare-kings draw is checked against the rules engine (f873988, 477a38d)
items.body: position.test.ts compares the computer's own bare-kings test with the engine's at every position of its random games; search.test.ts reaches the check in the quiet-move search. Deleting that check, or reading one side's material only, fails them. CLAUDE.md now lists this draw among those the search shares with the engine.

removed.intro: Production code is the same size: DR11 is +13 −13 lines and the worker fix +3 −1. The worker's coverage exclusion in vitest.config.ts is gone. Tests grew by about 400 lines, all of them checks shown to fail on broken code.

items.title: XR1 on the deployed site
items.body: The header is tested against the bench's model of how Pages reads _headers, not against Pages. Before the merge, at 22:40 UTC, curl -I https://3dchess.club/game/ABC123 returned x-frame-options: DENY (the /* rule) and no x-robots-tag, which is what the model predicts for the base. Ledger XR2 asks for the same check on production after the deploy.

items.title: damage.spec's bound on CI
items.body: The 0.25 median bound was set from local readings (at most 0.21). CI's software renderer may draw a move in fewer, larger frames, and the suite never retries. Ledger DS1: watch the PR's first CI runs.

items.title: The first Improve agent's list of breaks
items.body: Its commit said ten breaks; its list was lost in a container restart and the message names eight. The list was rebuilt in step 5 as 16 breaks covering every unit-level check of the run, and rerun on both sides.
